question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Bury the hatchet
solution:
The correct answer is: "**To end a quarrel**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• "**Bury the hatchet**" is an idiom that means to settle a dispute or end a quarrel. (किसी विवाद को निपटाने या झगड़ा ख़त्म करने के लिए)
 
• The phrase likely comes from the Native American tradition of burying a hatchet or tomahawk to symbolize the end of a conflict.
 
• Other similar idioms include "make peace," "call a truce," or "cease hostilities."
 
 
• **Example**: "*After years of feuding, the two families finally decided to bury the hatchet and reconcile.*"
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.
